summary.title: Day 12: Implementing Redis Protocol
summary.one_liner: You learn how to encode and decode the Redis Serialization Protocol (RESP) in Nim using a variant type for its five value kinds.
keywords: how to write a redis client
takeaways: RESP has five types: simple strings, errors, integers, bulk strings, and arrays, each marked by a leading byte and terminated by CRLF.
Redis clients send commands as arrays of bulk strings, e.g. GET USER becomes *2 followed by $3GET and $4USER.
A Nim variant object (RedisValue with a kind enum) can represent all RESP types, and encode/decode dispatch on the kind or first character.
Decoders return the parsed value plus the number of characters consumed, so arrays can be decoded recursively.
Null bulk strings use a length of -1 and are represented here with a placeholder value.
summary.summary: This is Day 12 of a Nim tutorial series that implements RESP, the Redis client-server protocol. The article explains the five RESP types and shows the expected encode and decode input/output examples. It then builds a RedisValue variant type in Nim, with encoder procedures for each type and a decoder that dispatches on the first character and recurses for arrays. It ends by showing how a command is turned into an array of bulk strings, and points to the nim-resp project it is based on.
